scenes.visual: Big navy hook text pops word by word; Norb peeks curious from below.
scenes.cardText: Why were you such a reckless teenager?
scenes.voiceover: Why were you so reckless as a teenager?

scenes.visual: Two pedals on a navy floor: GAS (coral) floored and vibrating with a thrill spark above; BRAKE (teal) half-built under mustard scaffolding. Norb jittery.
scenes.voiceover: Your brain has a gas pedal — the thrill-and-reward system — and brakes: the part that says 'wait, bad idea.' In your teens the gas is floored. But the brakes are still being installed.

scenes.visual: A teal brain whose front (behind the forehead) is wrapped in scaffolding with a swinging crane; the back glows finished. A WIRING pill. Norb panicked.
scenes.voiceover: That judgment part — right behind your forehead — is the last to finish wiring. So a teen feels the thrill at full blast while the brakes barely work.

scenes.visual: A coral urge wave swells high then crashes flat; a small navy anchor stands still, unbothered. Norb gets the idea.
scenes.voiceover: You can't rush the wiring. But the thrill always spikes and fades — so a pause, or a night's sleep, lets your brakes catch up.

scenes.visual: THE SCIENCE card; below it a 0-to-25 age axis sweeps left to right, and the prefrontal brain at the end only fills in at 25 with a BRAKES READY pill. Norb curious.
scenes.cardText: The prefrontal cortex — your brain's brakes — keeps wiring into your mid-twenties.
scenes.voiceover: The prefrontal cortex — the brain's brakes — keeps maturing into your mid-twenties. Brain scans show it is the last region to finish.

scenes.visual: TRY THIS card; below it the gas pedal floored beside the half-built brake. Norb celebrates.
scenes.cardText:
Big risk? Sleep on it.
Let your brakes catch up.
scenes.voiceover: So before any big risk: sleep on it. A rested brain brakes far better than a tired one — at any age.
